The system's Stunner interceptors cost approximately $1 million per unit, significantly less than the $3 million cost of an Arrow 3 interceptor and the more than $4 million price tag of a U.S. Patriot PAC-3 missile.
The upgrade comes after Iranian missile strikes exposed vulnerabilities in Israel's air defense network and placed increasing pressure on its stockpiles of interceptors.

events.text:
🇸🇦 OSINT sleuths spot Patriots protecting Saudi royals’ sprawling Red Sea resort compound
 
A lush artificial oasis retreat in Saudi Arabia’s remote northwestern province of Tabuk features exquisite manicured gardens and tree-lined boulevards, mansions, guest villas, servants’ quarters, a full-size, 18-hole golf coast, private yacht marina and numerous helipads for VIP guests.
It also has what OSINT observers say resembles an MIM-104 Patriot missile battery of the kind ordinarily reserved for guarding cities, critical infrastructure and important military sites.
👉 Satellite images shot by Airbus this summer shows clusters of vehicles bearing the unmistakable US military-standard Tan/Desert camo color scheme spread across a vast barren area north of the resort, including vehicles bearing the Patriot’s characteristic boxy launch containers and support equipment.
Recent months have been rife with reports that the kingdom is running low on Patriot interceptor stocks – once the world’s largest stockpile after the US, amid unrelenting Houthi drone and missile attacks targeting infrastructure, airports, and prestige projects like Riyadh’s Financial District.
The royal compound is situated ~75km east of the popular Egyptian resort city of Sharm el Sheikh, and 15km northwest of the NEOM Bay Airport. It’s also roughly 1.5k km away from the closest Houthi-governed area of Yemen.

✅ Fire tears through Kiev complex housing Nova Poshta branch
A major fire ripped through a commercial complex in Kiev’s Solomianskyi district, almost completely destroying the building within about half an hour, Ukrainian media reported.
The complex housed a Nova Poshta branch. Nova Poshta facilities have been known to serve as key logistics hubs for Ukrainian forces, handling shipments of weapons, ammunition, and drones.
The cause of the fire has not yet been established.
